text:
1	# LOOM portal: interface for agents
2	
3	This page is for an agent (or the developer of one) that needs part of a
4	person's health context to do a task for them. It is the only document an
5	agent needs; it does not have to read LOOM's source.
6	
7	## What LOOM offers
8	
9	LOOM holds one person's health record and hands out **task-scoped,
10	expiring slices** of it. You say what task you are doing; LOOM decides
11	how deep you may see, which fields you get, and for how long.
12	
13	| Tier | What it contains | Field names |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| L0 | raw sensor signal | `raw_signal` |
16	| L1 | readings (here: hourly glucose, mg/dL) | `readings` |
17	| L2 | patterns and alerts derived from readings | `glucose_patterns`, `alerts` |
18	| L3 | plain-language constraints | `constraints` |
19	
20	L0 is the deepest (most revealing), L3 the shallowest. A tier includes the
21	shallower ones: an L2 grant may carry `constraints` too.
22	
23	## Access
24	
25	- Base URL and namespace are given to you by whoever runs the portal (for
26	  a test: `http://127.0.0.1:8787` and a namespace such as `demo`).
27	  Every call for one person goes to `/v1/<namespace>/...`.
28	- There is no login in v0.1. You identify yourself with `agent_id` (this
29	  agent instance) and `publisher` (the company or developer that ships
30	  it). In Nanda Town the gateway fills `agent_id` from the signed envelope;
31	  over plain HTTP both are claims.
32	- JSON in, JSON out. Errors are JSON `{"error": "..."}`; a malformed body
33	  gets HTTP 400 naming the missing fields.
34	
35	## Endpoints
36	
37	| Method and path | Use |
38	|---|---|
39	| `GET /health` | version and policy id |
40	| `POST /v1/<ns>/requests` | ask for access for a task; a grant carries data immediately |
41	| `POST /v1/<ns>/fetch` | get fresh data again under a grant you already hold |
42	| `GET /v1/<ns>/credit` | publisher → credit score (only publishers that have been seen) |
43	| `GET /v1/<ns>/log` | the person's audit log: every decision, without the data (owner token only; agents get 403) |
44	| `GET /v1/policy` | the built-in tasks, as JSON (same as the table below) |
45	| `GET /v1/<ns>/proposals/<proposal_id>` | status of a proposal for a task that is not built in (see below) |
46	
47	### `POST /v1/<ns>/requests`: body
48	
49	| Field | Required | Meaning |
50	|---|---|---|
51	| `request_id` | yes | unique per request; reuse it only to retry the same request |
52	| `agent_id` | yes | your agent instance |
53	| `publisher` | yes | who ships you |
54	| `category` | yes | `agent_for_user` (works for the person) or `care_provider` (clinician side) |
55	| `task` | yes | one of the task names below |
56	| `purpose` | no | free text, recorded |
57	| `tier` | yes | the deepest tier you ask for (`L0`..`L3`) |
58	| `fields` | yes | list of field names you ask for |
59	| `at` | yes | current time on the person's timeline, in days (number) |
60	
61	### Tasks (policy `loom-policy-0.2.1`)
62	
63	| `task` | `category` | Deep

input.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/health; echo; curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/coldstart-3/requests -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"request_id":"chef1-mp-001","agent_id":"chef-1","publisher":"plateplan","category":"agent_for_user","task":"meal_plan","purpose":"plan dinners for the next 3 days tuned to glucose behavior","tier":"L2","fields":["glucose_patterns","constraints"],"at":0}' | python3 -m json.tool

input.command:
mkdir -p /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run3/out && cat > /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run3/out/chef-1.md <<'EOF'
# Dinner plan: days 1-3

> **Please confirm before I go further.** LOOM marked this as a first request
> from plateplan (`confirmation: first_request`), so you need to OK this plan
> before it's treated as final or used for anything else (like a shopping order).
> Reply "OK" or tell me what to change.

## What I'm tuning for

Over the last 14 days your glucose has been steady overall (average 127 mg/dL,
variability 14.8%, 100% of the time in range), but meals push you up to a peak
of about **177 mg/dL**. That's still in range, but close to the top of it. So
the job for dinner is to keep the after-meal spike lower, not to overhaul
anything. Your constraints are **limit added sugar** and **prefer low-glycemic
foods**.

How each dinner does that:

- **Half the plate is non-starchy veg, a quarter protein, a quarter (or less)
  slow carbs** (legumes, barley, quinoa, whole-grain or al dente pasta), and
  never white rice, white bread or potatoes as the main carb.
- **Eat it in order:** veg/salad first, then protein, carbs last. That reliably
  softens the spike.
- **Fat, fibre and acid** (olive oil, nuts, vinegar or lemon) in every meal to
  slow how fast the carbs are absorbed.
- **No added sugar** in sauces or marinades, and no dessert built on sugar.
  If you want something sweet, have berries with plain Greek yogurt.
- **A 10-15 minute walk after dinner** if you can. Moving your muscles after
  eating is one of the easiest ways to cut the peak.

## Day 1: Lemon-herb salmon, lentils and greens

- Baked salmon (about 150 g) with lemon, dill and olive oil
- Warm green or Puy lentils (about ¾ cup cooked) with shallot and a splash of red-wine vinegar
- Roasted broccoli and a big handful of rocket
- Start with the greens, finish with the lentils.

*Why:* lentils are among the lowest-GI carbs there are, and the omega-3 fat in
the salmon plus the vinegar both slow digestion.

## Day 2: Chicken and vegetable stir-fry over barley

- Chicken thigh (about 150 g) or firm tofu, stir-fried with peppers, snap peas, mushrooms, bok choy, garlic and ginger
- Sauce: soy or tamari, rice vinegar, sesame oil and chili. **No honey, sugar, hoisin or sweet chili sauce** (they're where stir-fries hide added sugar)
- Pearl barley (about ½ cup cooked) in place of white rice, or cauliflower rice mixed half-and-half with it
- Top with toasted cashews or sesame seeds

*Why:* barley's soluble fibre (beta-glucan) gives a much flatter curve than
white rice, and a sauce with no sugar takes away the second source of the spike.

## Day 3: Turkey-bean chili with a side salad

- Lean ground turkey (or more beans for a vegetarian version) with kidney beans and black beans, tomatoes, onion, peppers, courgette, cumin and smoked paprika
- Top with avocado, a spoon of plain Greek yogurt, and lime
- Side salad with olive oil and vinegar. Eat it first
- Skip the cornbread and tortilla chips. If you want a crunch, use a few pumpkin seeds

*Why:* beans give a lot of protein and fibre for their carbs, and avocado adds
fat. It also makes leftovers, which helps on a busy night.

## Quick swaps
| Instead of | Use |
|---|---|
| White rice / potatoes | Barley, quinoa, lentils, beans, cauliflower rice |
| Sweet sauces (teriyaki, BBQ, hoisin) | Tamari + vinegar + garlic/ginger; spice rubs |
| Juice / soda with dinner | Water, sparkling water with lime, unsweetened tea |
| Sugary dessert | Berries + plain Greek yogurt, a few nuts |

*This is a meal plan, not medical advice. If your clinician has given you
specific carb or glucose targets, those come first.*

## What I got from LOOM and how I used it

- **Request:** task `meal_plan`, category `agent_for_user`, tier L2, fields
  `glucose_patterns` + `constraints`. That's exactly what this task allows, so I
  didn't ask for raw readings (L1), the raw signal (L0) or alerts. The request
  was **granted** (grant `g-2aa5ed2dc6`, valid until day 7, can be fetched
  again). plateplan's credit went from 60 to 61. Friction band is medium, which
  means **you must confirm on this first request**. That's why the plan opens by
  asking for your OK.
- **Data received:** a 14-day window with mean 127 mg/dL, CV 14.8%, after-meal
  peak 177 mg/dL and 100% time in range. Constraints were `limit_added_sugar`
  and `prefer_low_glycemic`.
- **How I used it:** the after-meal peak (177) was the main thing I tuned for.
  It led to low-GI carbs in small portions, the veg-first eating order,
  fat/fibre/acid in every meal, and the walk after dinner. The steady mean and
  CV are why the changes are moderate, not restrictive. The two constraints
  ruled out sweetened sauces and sugar-based desserts, and set which carbs I
  picked.
- **What I didn't get or do:** I didn't have per-meal readings, so I can't
  say which of your own past dinners caused the 177 peak. The plan is tuned to
  the overall pattern, not to particular foods. I made no further fetches and
  kept no data outside this plan.
EOF
echo done

input.message:
I wrote a 3-day dinner plan tuned to the person's glucose. It's at /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run3/out/chef-1.md and ends with the "What I got from LOOM and how I used it" section.

I made one request to the LOOM portal (namespace coldstart-3, day 0) as agent chef-1, publisher plateplan. It was for task `meal_plan`, category `agent_for_user`, tier L2, fields `glucose_patterns` and `constraints`, which is exactly what that task allows. It was granted (grant g-2aa5ed2dc6, valid to day 7), and plateplan's credit went from 60 to 61. Over 14 days the person's glucose averaged 127 mg/dL with 14.8% variability and was in range 100% of the time, but peaks after meals reached about 177 mg/dL. Their constraints are `limit_added_sugar` and `prefer_low_glycemic`. Because steadiness is fine and the after-meal peak is the problem, the plan targets that peak without restricting much:
- **Day 1:** salmon with lentils and greens.
- **Day 2:** chicken or tofu stir-fry over barley, with a sugar-free sauce.
- **Day 3:** turkey and bean chili with avocado and a side salad.

Each dinner keeps carbs small and low-glycemic, adds fat, fibre and acid (oil, nuts, vinegar or lemon), has no added sugar, and comes with eat-veg-first and a 10-15 minute walk afterwards. LOOM flagged this as a first request (`confirmation: first_request`), meaning the person must confirm before anyone acts on the data, so the plan opens by asking for their OK. I made no extra fetches, didn't ask for raw readings, and opened no files besides the interface doc. One limit: without per-meal readings, the plan follows the overall pattern rather than which of their own dinners caused the spikes.
